subject: A leaf-covered path winding back into a misty autumn birch wood, framed by white birch trunks on both sides, with a low sun glowing through golden leaves at the upper left.
focal_point: Where the path disappears into the blue mist between the far pines and the mossy rock, framed by the two leaning birches on the left and the two birches on the right.
light: A low, hazy sun at the upper left, behind the trees. Its rays slant down to the right through the mist; every trunk is lit on its left side and shaded on its right, and the leaves catch the light on their upper left.
why: Cover the whole canvas with the glowing sky first, then build the wood from the back: the misty far pines and birches, the veil of mist and rays over them, the leafy ground, the bushes and the rock. The birches are the subject, so they get their own stage with base, shade, bark marks, branches and light as separate steps, and only then do the golden leaves go on over them, darkest first, ending with the sunlit taps and the glow around the sun.

things.name: The glowing, misty sky behind the wood
things.why: A soft gradient from warm gold at the upper left to cool misty blue at the right, blended wet in one go and run down the whole canvas behind everything.

things.name: The sun
things.why: A small, flat, near-white disk; one simple circle in one step.

things.name: The misty far pines
things.why: Evergreens stamped with a fan brush; being far and misty they stay flat blue-gray, so the optional light-side step is left out.
things.left_out: The light-side taps on the pines: in the mist they read as one flat cool shape.

things.name: The thin far birches in the mist
things.why: They are birches too, with a few dark marks, but far away: only the pale trunk and a few soft marks, no shading or light (both optional).
things.left_out: Shading and light on the far trunks, and their twigs; the mist flattens them.

things.name: The mist and the sun rays
things.why: Clouds covers mist and haze dry-brushed over a sky that's already there; the rays are mist lit by the sun. It lacks slanted rays as such, so the lay-in is dry-brushed in long diagonal strokes from the sun rather than circles.
things.left_out: The middle 'light the tops' layer; the rays get only their base and the brightest touch at the end.

things.name: The forest floor and the path
things.why: A ground laid in horizontally, lighter at the back and darker in front, which is what field-grass does. It lacks a leaf-litter texture, so the fallen leaves are their own thing with dabbing passes instead of its grass step.
things.left_out: The grass-texture step: the floor's texture is the fallen leaves.

things.name: The golden undergrowth and bushes
things.why: Bushes behind the trunks on both sides of the path and the dull olive shrubs at the foot of the pines: leafy masses dabbed dark, then mid, then sunlit.

things.name: The mossy rock beside the path
things.why: A lumpy, not-round shape with a lit top and a shaded side, built from one oval and a few pieces, then shaded and lit.
things.left_out: Moss texture and cracks; three values are enough to make it a rock.

things.name: The five near birch trunks
things.why: The subject: pale trunks shaded on the right, broken dark bark marks, and light on the left, exactly the birch element's four steps.
things.left_out: The papery peel and fine texture inside the bark; the marks are one repeated broken stroke.

things.name: The dark branches of the near birches
things.why: Dark branches pulled out from the trunks into the canopy, thick at the trunk and tapering.
things.left_out: The light on the branches and the fine twigs; the leaves cover most of them.

things.name: The golden leaf canopy
things.why: Masses of golden leaves across the top of the canvas and hanging over the trunks: dabbed dark, mid, then sunlit.
things.left_out: Individual leaf shapes; the canopy is three passes of dabs.

things.name: The fallen leaves on the ground and path
things.why: The closest element: fallen leaves are leaves in a mass and built the same way, dark, mid, then sunlit dabs. It lacks a ground version, so the dabs are laid flatter and wider in front and smaller toward the far path.
things.left_out: Leaf shapes and veins; the leaves are flat dabs.

paints.name: Pale gold
paints.looks: a pale warm yellow (white, yellow and a touch of red), the glow of the sky and the sunlit leaves

paints.name: Sun cream
paints.looks: almost white with a hint of warmth (Pale gold plus lots of white), the sun and the brightest glow

paints.name: Misty blue
paints.looks: a soft, light gray-blue (white, ultramarine, a touch of burnt sienna), the far air

paints.name: Pine blue-gray
paints.looks: a dark slate blue with a little green (ultramarine, burnt sienna, a little yellow and white), the nearer far pines

paints.name: Birch gray-white
paints.looks: a pale cool gray-white (white with a touch of ultramarine and burnt sienna), the birch bark

paints.name: Bark umber
paints.looks: a near-black warm brown (burnt sienna and ultramarine), the bark marks and branches

paints.name: Birch shadow gray
paints.looks: a mid gray with a hint of brown (Birch gray-white darkened with a little Bark umber), the shaded side of the trunks

paints.name: Bright birch white
paints.looks: a warm near-white (Birch gray-white plus white and a whisper of yellow), the sunlit edge of the trunks

paints.name: Leaf-litter rust
paints.looks: a warm orange-brown (burnt sienna, red and yellow), the leafy floor

paints.name: Pale rust
paints.looks: a light dusty tan (Leaf-litter rust plus white), the path and the misty back of the floor

paints.name: Dark rust
paints.looks: a deep red-brown (Leaf-litter rust plus a little Bark umber), the front of the floor and the trunk shadows

paints.name: Moss gray-green
paints.looks: a dull olive gray-green (yellow, ultramarine, burnt sienna and white), the shrubs by the pines and the rock

paints.name: Dark moss
paints.looks: a deep olive-slate (Moss gray-green plus a little ultramarine), the rock's shaded side

paints.name: Pale moss
paints.looks: a light yellow-olive (Moss gray-green plus white and a little yellow), the moss on the rock's lit top

paints.name: Burnt orange
paints.looks: a deep orange-brown (red, yellow and burnt sienna), the shadowed leaves

paints.name: Golden yellow
paints.looks: a strong golden yellow (yellow with a touch of red), the main color of the leaves

steps.name: Blend the glowing sky over the whole canvas

lays.what: the whole canvas: Sun cream around where the sun will be at the upper left, Pale gold spreading out from it over the left half, blending into Misty blue across the right half and the top right, run all the way to the bottom edge

steps.after: The whole canvas is covered: a soft glow, near-white at the upper left, warm gold across the left, turning to a cool misty blue on the right and top right, with no white canvas left. Nothing else is painted yet.
steps.why: Everything else sits in this air; running it to the bottom keeps the strokes long and leaves no white behind the trees.

steps.name: Circle in the sun

lays.what: a small near-white disk at the upper left, a little in from the left edge, about a sixth of the way down

steps.after: A soft, round, near-white sun sits in the gold glow at the upper left. The rest of the canvas is the flat blended sky.
steps.why: The sun is the farthest thing, so it goes on the dry sky before anything passes in front of it.

steps.name: Stamp the misty far pines

lays.what: a cluster of pines right of center, from about a third of the way down to just above the middle: the nearer, taller ones in Pine blue-gray, the ones behind them paler in Misty blue, each stamped from the tip down and widening

steps.after: Right of center a group of soft blue-gray pine shapes rises into the misty blue, the nearest ones darker, the rest fading back. The left side is still the gold glow and the sun.
steps.why: The farthest solid things; they set the cool depth the path leads into.

steps.name: Pull the thin far birches

lays.what: six or so thin pale trunks standing in the middle distance, from the top of the canvas down to just above the middle, between where the near trunks will go and in front of the pines; the ones deeper in the mist paler and bluer

steps.after: Thin, pale gray-white trunks stand across the middle of the canvas, a little wider at their feet, the farthest ones nearly lost in the blue. They are plain pale lines, no marks yet.
steps.why: They stand in front of the pines and behind the mist.

steps.name: Line the soft marks on the far birches

lays.what: a few short, broken dark marks across each far trunk, more toward the bottom, softer and sparser than on the near trunks

steps.after: The far trunks now read as birches, each with a few small dark dashes, mostly low down. They stay pale and soft, with lots of plain gray-white between the marks.
steps.why: Done before the mist so the mist softens them.

steps.name: Dry-brush the mist and the sun rays

lays.what: long diagonal rays of Sun cream and Pale gold slanting down to the right from the sun across the left third, and a veil of Misty blue dragged over the feet of the pines and far birches

steps.after: Soft, broken pale rays fan down from the sun across the left side, and the bottoms of the far pines and birches fade into blue haze. The far wood looks misty and deep; the lower half is still plain sky color.
steps.why: Mist sits in front of the far wood and behind everything near.

stages.name: The forest floor and the bushes

steps.name: Lay in the forest floor and the path

lays.what: the lower half of the canvas in Leaf-litter rust, with a Pale rust path that starts wide at the bottom center and narrows as it winds back up to the middle, just right of center, and the back of the floor lighter in Pale rust

steps.after: The bottom half is a warm rust floor with a lighter tan path winding back to the middle. The back of the floor is pale and soft where it meets the mist. No leaves, bushes or trunks yet.
steps.why: The ground goes in before everything that stands on it.

steps.name: Darken the front of the floor and the trunk shadows

lays.what: the bottom quarter, and the long shadows that slant across the path toward the viewer from where the trunks will stand

steps.after: The front of the floor and a few broad bands across the path are a deep red-brown; the floor now goes from dark in front to pale tan at the back, and the path still shows light between the shadows.
steps.why: The shadows go under the leaves, so they come before them.

steps.name: Dab the dark of the undergrowth

lays.what: loose bushes along the back of the floor on both sides of the path, rising highest at the left and at the right edge, in Burnt orange; the dull shrubs at the foot of the pines and behind the rock in Moss gray-green

steps.after: Rough, dark orange-brown bush shapes sit along the back of the floor on both sides of the path, with olive shrubs under the pines. The mist and floor show through the gaps.
steps.why: The bushes are behind the near trunks, so they go on now; the Moss gray-green is mixed now for the rock next.

steps.name: Dab golden yellow on the bushes

lays.what: golden yellow taps over most of each bush, more on their upper left, leaving the dark showing at the bottoms

steps.after: The bushes glow golden yellow on top with dark orange-brown left at their bases and in the gaps. The olive shrubs by the pines stay dull.
steps.why: Middle value of the bushes while the dark is fresh in mind; the sunlit taps come at the end with the other leaves.

steps.name: Build the mossy rock from pieces

lays.what: a low lumpy rock right of the path, just below the middle: one flat oval first, then a smaller rounded piece on each side

steps.after: A flat olive gray-green rock shape sits on the floor right of the path, in front of the bushes. It is one flat color.
steps.why: It sits on the floor in front of the bushes.

steps.name: Shade the rock's right side and base

lays.what: the right side and the bottom of the rock, curving with its form

steps.after: The rock is darker on its right and along the bottom where it meets the ground; the olive still shows on its top and left.
steps.why: Light comes from the left, so the right is in shadow.

steps.name: Dry-brush the moss light on the rock's top

lays.what: the top and upper left of the rock

steps.after: A broken yellow-olive light lies across the top left of the rock, smaller than the olive under it, with the dark right side untouched. The rock looks round and mossy.
steps.why: Third value; keeps the highlight on the light side.

steps.name: Pull the five pale birch trunks

lays.what: five trunks from the top edge to the floor: a slim one near the left edge, two thick ones leaning right just left of center, one right of center and the thickest near the right edge; each wider at its foot and tapering up

steps.after: Five pale gray-white trunks stand over everything from top to bottom, framing the path, two leaning on the left and two upright on the right with a slim one at far left. They are flat pale shapes with no shading or marks.
steps.why: The subject goes on over the dry background; this is the ugly stage, so tell the painter it's normal.

steps.name: Dry-brush the shade down the right of each trunk

lays.what: the right side of every trunk, and darker toward the feet

steps.after: Each trunk now has a gray shaded right side and gets grayer near the ground, so it looks round; the left side is still pale.
steps.why: Shade before marks, so the marks sit over the round form.

steps.name: Lay the broken dark bark marks and the dark at the feet

lays.what: short, broken dark marks across each trunk with the brush's edge, many only partway across, denser toward the base, and the near-black at the foot of every trunk where it meets the ground

steps.after: Every trunk carries uneven dark bark marks, sparse and small high up and heavy at the bottom, and each foot is dark where it enters the leaves. Plenty of pale bark shows between the marks.
steps.why: The marks go on a dry, shaded trunk so they don't smear gray.

steps.name: Pull the dark branches out from the trunks

lays.what: a few branches from the upper trunks reaching out and up into the top of the canvas: from the leaning left trunks toward the center top, and from the right trunks out to both sides

steps.after: Dark branches fork out from the upper trunks into the sky, thick where they leave the trunk and tapering. The top of the canvas is still the sky, ready for leaves.
steps.why: Branches go under the canopy, so before the leaves; Bark umber is still on the palette.

steps.name: Catch the light on the left of each trunk

lays.what: a near-white stripe dragged down the left side of every trunk, over some of the dry marks

steps.after: Each trunk now has a bright left edge, a pale middle and a gray right side, with the dark marks broken by light in places. The birches look round and sunlit.
steps.why: Last value of the subject, on the side facing the sun.

steps.name: Dab the dark leaves in the canopy and on the floor

lays.what: loose clumps of dark leaves across the top of the canvas, hanging over the branches and the tops of the trunks, thickest at the top left and top right
scattered dark leaf dabs over the whole floor and path, wide and flat in front, smaller and closer toward the far end of the path

steps.after: Dark orange-brown leaf clumps hang across the top over the branches, with sky showing between them, and dark leaf dabs are scattered over the floor and path, over the feet of the trunks. The leaves are all one dark color.
steps.why: One loaded brush, one tap, one mix: the shadow leaves above and below are the same color and the same mark.

steps.name: Dab golden yellow over the canopy and the floor

lays.what: golden yellow taps over most of each canopy clump, more on the upper left, leaving dark showing underneath
golden yellow dabs over most of the floor, thickest at the sides and in front, fewer on the path, leaving dark between them

steps.after: The canopy and the floor are now mostly golden yellow, with the burnt orange showing in gaps and under the clumps. The path still shows its tan and dark shadows between the leaves.
steps.why: Same brush, same mix, same tap above and below; the middle value of every leaf.

steps.name: Tap the sunlit leaves everywhere

lays.what: a few pale gold taps on the upper left of the canopy clumps, most near the sun
a few pale gold taps on the tops of the bushes at the left and along the back
pale gold dabs in the sunny patches along the path and in front, between the trunk shadows

steps.after: Small pale gold lights sparkle on the lit side of the canopy, on the tops of the bushes and in sunny patches along the path, covering less than the golden yellow, so the leaves look lit from the upper left.
steps.why: The light the sun puts on every leaf is one loaded brush and one tap; it comes last so it sits on top.

steps.name: Brighten the glow around the sun

lays.what: a little near-white in small circles moving outward around the sun and along the top of the brightest rays, over any leaves that strayed into it

steps.after: The sun at the upper left glows bright with a soft halo, and the brightest rays stand out against the leaves. The painting is finished.
steps.why: The brightest light is the last touch.
